# chore(proposals): reconcile entry 2 against the incoming loom sync

**Commit**: `34919cf87395` — chore(proposals): reconcile entry 2 against the incoming loom sync

**Body**:

The 2026-08-02 Gate-2 sync (loom 43167a54921f) changed emit.mjs, one of this
proposal's three targets. Reconciling before merge — the third time this
session that checking a backlog item against ground truth changed its
disposition.

Entry 2 is superseded. validateTierCompleteness now opens with
`if (!isManifestOwnerClass(REPO))` and returns a skipReason naming the repo
class; the caller prints `[validator-15] tier-completeness: SKIP (...)`. The
diagnosis was right and the fix has landed upstream.

Worth recording rather than just deleting: this entry ORIGINALLY specified the
gate as "run ONLY where the repo distributes", which is fail-open — a missing
or corrupt VERSION would have skipped the validator, including at loom. This
cycle's redteam caught that and inverted it. Loom's independently-authored
implementation reached the same fail-closed answer by a stronger route:
isManifestOwnerClass THROWS on every unresolved class with the rationale "it
fails CLOSED rather than guess." Two independent derivations converging is
corroboration the polarity is right, and it is why the entry needs no
forwarding — loom's version is better than what this would have sent.

One sub-item is recorded as UNVERIFIED rather than covered: whether any
validator asserts the SKIP line's presence (so a path that neither runs nor
announces its skip is detectable) was not checked this cycle.

Entries 1 and 3 remain live — sync-from-template.md and sweep.md were not
touched by the sync.

Retained per artifact-flow.md append-never-overwrite; Gate-1 should SKIP
entry 2 as already-distributed rather than re-classify it.
